title: Design an onboarding flow that survives interruption
summary: Build a mobile-first three-step setup with validation, backtracking, draft recovery, and an honest network failure.
originNote: A conventional multi-step-flow control with loss prevention, accessibility, and recovery in tension with speed.

setup.instructions: Mount the fictional setup packet. Build a self-contained static application whose simulated persistence and failures work offline.

turns.content: Read fixtures/flow.json and implement the complete mobile-first setup flow as index.html. A user must be able to complete it by keyboard, go back without losing valid entries, reload midway and recover a local draft, and encounter the packet's simulated final-step failure without losing work. Validation must explain how to recover and move focus to a useful place. Include a visible 'Clear saved draft' action. Expose the active step as data-step and the failed submission region as data-state="submit-failed". Do not add accounts, marketing, or fields not in the packet.
Revise the flow so the optional update preference cannot block completion or masquerade as required consent. Preserve all entered data, recovery behavior, and the three-step structure.

checks.description: Draft clearing and simulated failure hooks are present.
Complete, backtrack, reload after step two, retry the simulated failure, and complete using only the keyboard.
